div.div:
1 طَرِزَ , aor.
طَرَزَ , (K,) inf. n. طَرَزٌ, (TK,) He became goodly in shape, form, or aspect, after having been thick. (Sgh, * K, * TK.) ―
-b2- (tropical:) He became good in disposition, after having been evil. (K.) ―
-b3- طَرِزَ فِى ٱلْمَلْبَسِ, (K,) and فِى ٱلْمَطْعَمِ, (TA,) (tropical:) He was nice, or dainty (تَأَنَّقَ, K, or تَنَوَّقَ, A) in apparel, (K, * TA,) and in diet; (TA;) not wearing, (K, TA,) and not eating, (TA,) aught but what was good: (K, TA:) as also فِيهِمَا ↓ تطرّز . (TA.) ＝
-A2- Accord. to IAar, الطَّّرْزُ signifies الرفع باللكز; [thus in the L and TA; but, I think, incorrectly, for الدَّفْعُ بِاللَّكْزِ;] and one says, طَرَزَهُ, inf. n. طَرْزٌ [app. meaning He repelled him by striking with his fist]. (L, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
